👆According to Note 3 of Article 27, "Producing artistic work without a permit from the country's legal institutions will result in six months to five years of prohibition from artistic activity and two to four times the production costs of the work." Of course, this does not mean that, for example, "if you paint a picture at home, you must first obtain a permit from the country's legal institutions," but the way it is written is so unprofessional that it allows for abuse and expansion of the concept of crime. The same applies to the very broad phrase "under the support, supervision, guidance, training, or direction of a foreign agent," under which anything can be interpreted as criminal. This scope is so wide that even repenting for a crime not committed becomes a crime; does the scripture of judgment and governance have no verse of mercy? The implementation of such a plan and the restrictions on independent internet media such as "Azad" completely eliminates the intermediate class of intellectual elites, takes political struggle to the blind instincts of the yellow layers of society, and drives the masses to the same place we saw in the bitter tragedies of Dey 1404. When you push honorable artists and intellectuals out of the arena with flimsy excuses, the way opens for those who win awards at international festivals by producing yellow and dark-portraying films and artistic works that misrepresent Iran's image. A class of yellow intellectuals and undereducated celebrities, through self-display, become hollow heroes for naive youth. The end result is clear; the enemies create sedition from "insubordination" and "weapons," and again you portray an inhuman image of Iran and the Islamic Republic, and before world public opinion, you become apologists for the warmongering of enemies. That's it.

entry.title: Two Separate Roles Our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, played two great…
entry.summary:
Source: @fazelimohammadir

Two Separate Roles
Our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, played two great roles in history.
His first role was prophetic. He presented his profound spiritual experience of the oneness of God, the universe, the afterlife, and the path to human happiness as a worldview in the form of verses focused on good conduct and individual and collective morality, to serve as a guide for seekers forever.
His second role was the political leadership of a small community, entrusted to him through an agreement by the people of Medina, which was distinct in nature from his prophetic role. Muhammad spent thirteen years in his birthplace, Mecca, as only a prophet, enduring much harassment and persecution from his people.
The last ten years of our Prophet's life, in addition to his prophetic mission, involved the political leadership of the people of Yathrib, which he renamed Medina—meaning the city or a center of civility and lawfulness as opposed to savagery and lawlessness.
The Prophet was a highly skilled, realistic, and capable political leader. As the demands of politics required, he made treaties, fought, made peace, forgave, took a hard line, retreated, and advanced.
The prophetic mission addresses humanity "as it ought to be," while political leadership manages humanity "as it is."
Hence, Muhammad's prophetic messages are a transhistorical and eternal legacy, while his political leadership is subject to the changing and evolving nature of the times, carrying all the complexities, tragedies, and necessary flexibilities of relative matters.
Our Prophet did not see political affairs as a pre-discovered and predetermined truth; he put them to consultation and made decisions through deliberation with the people of Medina. Some believers and non-believers in Muhammad's faith lack the ability to distinguish between these two roles, and thus misunderstand his great undertaking.
Ahmad Zeidabadi ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: Dear Azad audience, this conversation between Foad Izadi and Nasser Hadian…
entry.summary:
Source: @fazelimohammadir

Dear Azad audience, this conversation between Foad Izadi and Nasser Hadian should not be seen merely as a debate between representatives of two schools of thought. Nasser Hadian, as one of the most important figures who has played a role over decades in Track II (unofficial) negotiations with America, and Foad Izadi, as one of the most important radical critics in the discussion of an agreement with America, are not simply representatives of two viewpoints. They should be seen as ideologues, theorists, and of course activists of two opposing approaches; two approaches in the tension between which a significant part of Iran's policy toward America over the past few decades has been shaped, and whose consequences have affected the fate of Iranians. This conversation begins with a discussion of the roots of Iran-America enmity and proceeds to assess America's causes and goals in starting the war, possible changes in American policy, proposed solutions for Iran, and the consequences of each of these paths. From this perspective, what we see in front of the camera is an example of the very dialogue that has been ongoing for years in policy circles and behind closed doors. This 4-hour conversation, despite all its ups and downs, is a sympathetic effort by both sides to present the necessary arguments and evidence to explain two different views and two different solutions. We invite all experts and enthusiasts to help continue and develop this conversation by critiquing and judging the views and arguments presented. Ultimately, this conversation can be considered a historical document of one of the most important strategic disagreements in Iran's foreign policy; a document that may in the future allow for a more precise judgment about the results of pursuing or abandoning each of these two views. 🎞 Full video of this conversation on Azad's YouTube: https://youtu.be/LqQ-RfN8mWQ ✅ Support Azad in "foreign currency" and "rial" 🆔AzadSocial
